style: Monochrome architect sketch: objects, selective hatching, curved connectors, restrained hand-drawn contours, clear labels.
status: Approved visual direction for the Second Edition.

figures.title: Diagnose the queue
figures.caption: Read a sample of customer questions and distinguish product behavior, hard-to-find answers, repeatable tasks, and work needing human investigation.
figures.takeaway: Classified customer tasks and candidate fixes.

figures.title: Choose the machine
figures.caption: A support system has several layers. Buy, extend and build remain options at each layer; each component still needs funded operating ownership.
figures.takeaway: An owner, lifecycle cost and exit path for each component.

figures.title: Design the guardrails
figures.caption: The answer path uses applicable evidence. The action path separately checks permission, executes, and verifies a receipt. Missing evidence or authority leads to a stop or human handoff.
figures.takeaway: Allowed actions, evidence checks and a clear human exit.

figures.title: Shadow-run the machine
figures.caption: Give a human reference review and an isolated candidate run the same request-time evidence. Compare the results; the candidate has no live messaging or write capability.
figures.takeaway: A reviewed scorecard, observed failures and a release decision.

figures.title: Launch with direct accountability
figures.caption: Readiness checks lead to a bounded cutover and observation. Evidence supports continuing; stop conditions route to containment and a staffed human service path.
figures.takeaway: Named owners, cutover checks and tested recovery capacity.

figures.title: Operate the living system
figures.caption: Customer evidence moves through review, an accountable owner, a tested change, release, and a later outcome check. The evidence feeds the next iteration.
figures.takeaway: An assigned owner, a tested change and later evidence of its effect.

figures.title: The 16% problem
figures.caption: Of 100 eligible conversations, an agent is involved in 40. If 40 percent of those 40 are reported resolved, that is 16 of the original 100. These are illustrative counts, not company results.
figures.placement: Chapter 18 — CSAT and Other Comfort Metrics
figures.takeaway: Reported resolution still needs a separate customer-outcome check.

figures.title: Evaluation over time
figures.caption: Check related returns seven and thirty days after reported resolution. Each denominator needs a mature observation window and known coverage. Weekly independent answer review runs on a separate track.
figures.placement: Chapter 28 — Evaluating AI: The Work Is Never Done
figures.takeaway: Customer silence alone does not prove success.

figures.title: When the effect is unknown
figures.caption: An authorized attempt can leave an uncertain effect. Inspect provider state or assign a human owner before deciding what to retry. If a credit succeeded but its confirmation failed, recover the message without issuing another credit.
figures.placement: Chapter 16 — Did the Action Actually Happen?
figures.takeaway: Recover the unfinished step without duplicating a completed effect.

figures.title: From goalkeeper to midfield
figures.caption: Support engineers keep a staffed human recovery path and spend protected time improving documentation, product behavior and onboarding to prevent repeated customer problems.
figures.takeaway: Protected improvement time, product access and a staffed human path.
